defs.def: a word or phrase used to describe sb/sth else, in a way that is different from its normal use, in order to show that the two things have the same qualities and to make the description more powerful, for example She has a heart of stone; the use of such words and phrases 暗喻；隐喻

ex.s: Maya Angelou explained she first heard the "rainbow in the clouds" metaphor in a 19th-century African-American song.
ex.t: 玛雅·安吉罗解释说，她第一次听到“云中彩虹”这个比喻，是在一首 19 世纪的非洲裔美国人的歌曲中。

ex.s: It is suddenly clear that when the clock masters say that “these antiques have lives”, it is neither an exaggeration nor a metaphor.
ex.t: 突然很明显，当钟表大师说“这些古董有生命”时，既不是夸张，也不是隐喻。

ex.s: Similes and metaphors are two commonly used, but easy to confuse, figures of speech.
ex.t: 明喻和隐喻是两种常用但容易混淆的修辞手法。

ex.s: Unlike similes, metaphors make direct comparisons without using connecting words.
ex.t: 与比喻不同，隐喻在不使用连接词的情况下进行直接比较。

ex.s: An extended metaphor refers to a comparison between two things that is developed at length over many lines of text, or throughout an entire work of literature.
ex.t: 扩展隐喻是指在许多文本行或整个文学作品中详细发展的两件事物之间的比较。
